title: Integrated Security & Compliance Guidance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exceptions
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational workflows for role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC gating, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence collection, and handling of risk & exceptions. It is intended for engineers, platform owners, product security reviewers, and audit stakeholders who implement or verify controls for production systems.

Scope & Purpose

- Scope: Applies to all Redwood-managed control plane services, hosted inference endpoints, Dedicated pools, and Private deployment artifacts (control-plane components, configuration management, CI artifacts, and audit evidence).
- Purpose: Provide a single reference describing control requirements, operational runbooks, review cadences, and authority matrix for exceptions.

Ownership and Roles

- Security (policy owner): overall policy, annual compliance attestations, exception approvals for high-risk systems.
- Eng-SRE: enforce runtime controls, logging pipelines, alerting, and quarterly access reviews.
- Eng-Infra: identity and provisioning integrations, secrets management, network controls.
- Product / Platform: maintain system-level documentation, access onboarding approvals, and ensure secure SDLC gates are met before production rollout.

RBAC & Authentication

Principles
- Least privilege by default: roles grant minimum permissions needed for tasks.
- Role-based groups: no broad 'admin' role with multi-system permissions unless business-approved.
- Identity source of truth: use corporate identity (Okta) for SSO; all access must be traceable to a user or service principal.

Roles & Permissioning (examples)
- viewer (read-only): list and read resources, inability to modify production configs.
- operator: deploy/run actions limited to scoped services (e.g., dedicated-gpu-cluster management).
- infra-admin: provision infra resources, change network routes (requires two-person approval for sensitive actions).
- security-admin: audit log configuration, evidence export, exception approval visibility.

Provisioning & Lifecycle
1. Onboarding: manager/owner requests group membership via self-serve Access Portal; request must include justification and expiration date (max 90 days per request).
2. Approval: team lead and designated approver from platform/security.
3. Temporary escalation: timeboxed elevated access requires ticket in access tracking system and automated revocation.
4. Deprovisioning: automated offboarding on identity provider change; weekly sync job reconciles group membership.

Periodic Reviews
- Access reviews run quarterly for all high-privilege groups (infra-admin, security-admin).
- Review SLA: reviewers must complete within 14 days. Non-responders escalate to the group owner.

Authentication & Service Identity
- All services must use short-lived service tokens issued by the internal CA or workload identity (OIDC) provider.
- Secrets must live in the approved Secrets Manager (HashiCorp Vault / cloud KMS) and be referenced by templated injection; no plaintext secrets in repo.

Audit Logging

Objectives
- Ensure tamper-evident, centralized collection of audit events for authentication, authorization decisions, configuration changes, model onboarding, deployment actions, and data access.

What we log (minimum required)
- Authentication: login success/fail, MFA events, token issuance/revocation.
- Authorization: RBAC allow/deny decisions, policy changes, group assignments.
- Admin actions: infrastructure changes, IAM policy edits, model version rollouts, key rotations.
- Data access: reads/exports of customer data or PII-labeled assets.
- System alerts: anomaly detections and major error surfaces.

Logging Architecture & Retention
- Pipeline: event producers -> secure collector (TLS, mTLS where supported) -> aggregator -> long-term store.
- Ingestion latency target: <= 2 minutes for critical audit events (SLO).
- Retention: critical security logs (authentication and authorization events) retained for 7 years for regulated customers; default organizational retention is 13 months for operational logs.
- Integrity: write-once storage for immutable logs where possible; log signing applied at aggregation layer.

Access and Monitoring
- Log access restricted to security and designated auditors; access requires role membership and approval.
- Real-time alerts: predefined detection rules (e.g., brute-force, anomalous admin actions) generate PagerDuty incidents routed to SecOps.
- Audit export process: approved exports are tracked with justification and export artifact hashed and stored in Evidence Repository.

Data Residency & Retention

Policy Rules
- Customer data (payloads, embeddings, files) stored only in the regions explicitly selected by the customer; default is us-west-2 for new accounts unless otherwise requested.
- Control-plane metadata may replicate across regions for reliability but PII must follow residency constraints.

Classification & Retention Table (minimum)
| Data Type | Residency | Retention | Owner |
|-----------|----------:|----------:|------|
| Auth logs (critical) | Regional copies + global index | 7 years (compliance) | Security |
| Operational traces | Multi-region | 13 months | Eng-SRE |
| Customer payloads | Customer-selected region(s) | per-customer policy (30-3650 days) | Customer Data Owner |
| CI artifacts | us-west-2 | 180 days | Eng-Infra |

Retention Enforcement
- Automated retention jobs enforce deletion policies; deletion must produce proof-of-deletion artifacts (timestamp and checksum).
- For deletions in Private/on-prem deployments, on-prem operator must complete retention checklist and upload evidence to the Evidence Repository.

Secure SDLC Requirements

Gating & Pre-Production Controls
- All production-bound changes must pass: automated unit + integration tests, static analysis (SAST), dependency scanning, and secrets scanning.
- PR policy: at least 1 code owner review + 1 security reviewer for infra changes and model onboarding PRs.
- CI job requirements: run tests in ephemeral runners, sign build artifacts, and publish SBOM for each release.

Release Controls
- Canary rollouts for model/version changes with automated rollback on quality/regression criteria.
- Production deploy requires an associated deployment checklist: release notes, security sign-off (where required), monitoring dashboard, and rollback plan.

Secrets & Key Management
- KMS-managed keys only; hardware-backed keys (HSM) required for customer encryption keys when requested.
- Periodic key rotation per policy (yearly for encryption keys, 90 days for short-lived service tokens).

Incident Response - Security Procedures

Detection & Triage
1. Detection: alerts from monitoring, IDS, or third-party reports.
2. Triage: SecOps performs triage within 30 minutes of a critical alert (SLO), determines severity.

Escalation Matrix & Roles
- Incident Commander (IC): security oncall (default) until SOC hands to Eng-Lead for service-specific incidents.
- Forensic Lead: appointed when endpoint or potential data exfiltration is suspected.
- Communications Lead: owns internal and external communications, coordinates with Legal and Customer Success for customer notifications.

Containment & Forensics (runbook excerpt)
1. Capture volatile state: memory snapshots, live process lists, network connections (document times and hashes).
2. Isolate affected hosts/services via network policy or service-level toggle.
3. Preserve logs: snapshot relevant audit/log streams and create an export artifact with integrity metadata.
4. If customer data exposure suspected: notify Legal and Customer Success within 2 hours and follow notification playbook.
5. Post-incident: complete a security postmortem with root cause, timeline, mitigation, and action items; submit to Incident Review board.

Communication & Regulatory Reporting
- For incidents meeting regulatory thresholds (e.g., PII exposure), Security with Legal will prepare required filings (e.g., GDPR/CCPA notifications) and timeline-driven actions.
- Public status updates handled via Status Page and coordinated statements; sensitive details redacted as necessary.

Compliance Evidence Workflows

Artifacts and Storage
- Evidence types: access review logs, audit exports, change approvals, deployment checklists, SBOMs, test results, vulnerability scan outputs, exception approvals.
- Evidence Repository: immutable storage with per-artifact metadata (who, when, justification, hash).

Collection & Audit Support Process
1. Evidence request received from auditor or internal reviewer.
2. Security curator assembles artifacts, validates integrity (hash), and provides read-only export with timeboxed access.
3. All evidence access logged and reviewed.

Attestation Cadence
- Quarterly internal attestations for high-risk systems.
- Annual third-party audit (SOC2/ISO) evidence package prepared by Security with input from Eng teams.

Risk & Exceptions

Exception Process
1. Submit exception request with risk assessment, compensating controls, and expiration date (max 365 days).
2. Security reviews and routes to Exception Board if risk is > medium.
3. Approval matrix: Security (<= medium risk), Exception Board (> medium), CFO/Legal (high strategic risk).
4. Approved exceptions recorded in Exception Registry with enforced expiry and automated reminders 30/7 days before expiry.

Compensating Controls (examples)
- Enhanced monitoring and increased log retention for resources excluded from standard controls.
- Network isolation and short-lived access tokens with strict MFA for temporary exceptions.

Risk Metrics & Reporting
- Key metrics tracked: number of open exceptions, average time to close exception, overdue access reviews, and evidence gaps.
- Dashboards refreshed daily and reviewed in Quarterly Risk Review with Executive stakeholders.
